newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ergo expects NZ floating rates to rise over 1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ergo expects NZ floating rates to rise over 1 pct.

text.p: Ergo Managing Director Graham Meyer told Radio New Zealand on Tuesday that variable mortgage rates would have to rise by more than one percentage point if wholesale rates stay around current levels.
The no-frills home lender currently offers a variable and one-year fixed lending rate of 8.25 percent against the 90-day bank bill rate of 8.62.
"There will have to be a significant increase in both the floating home rate and some of the fixed home loan rates.
"It's just a matter of when at this stage," he said.
Ergo was holding off to see if wholesale rates would correct.

"But if rates were to remain at their current level of about 8.45 percent or 8.42, my view is that there would need to be a rise of at least one percent in the home loan rate for both variable home loans and for fixed rates."
Meyer said it was hard to know if the rise in wholesale rates was a short-term phenomenon.
He said confidence in the business sector and with consumers was already fragile.
"A rise of this order will have a very adverse effect on people's confidence," he said.
